title: Terraform module sandbox testcases and backcompat matrix
body:
Purpose:
This doc collects a focused set of sandbox testcases, acceptance criteria, and a backwards-compatibility matrix for the VPC/IAM/cluster (EKS/GKE/AKS) terraform primitives used in private deployments. The goal is to provide a pragmatic, repeatable checklist teams can run in CI (or locally) before merging module changes that touch public inputs/outputs or state shaping behavior.

Context / motivation:
- We've had several rollbacks caused by subtle output name changes and implicit behavior shifts when modules were upgraded in customer clusters.
- Private deployments span cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) + on-prem templates; differences in networking primitives and IAM semantics mean tests must be explicit and cross-cloud aware.
- This doc intentionally targets small, fast sandbox testcases that run in our sandbox cloud accounts or local k8s where possible (kind, kubeadm) rather than long end-to-end customer installs.

Principles (non‑negotiable):
- Non-breaking: modules must preserve stable public outputs and variable semantics for patch bumps (semver: patch = bugfix, minor = additive nonbreaking, major = breaking).
- Idempotent: repeated apply/destroy cycles in the sandbox must converge (no drift-caused resources left behind).
- Observable: testcases must assert on module outputs, resource counts, and at least one runtime smoke check (e.g., cluster node readiness, route propagation).
- Reproducible: tests use deterministic inputs; where randomness is required a seed must be recorded.

Folder expectations for module repo (CI mapping):
- /tests/sandbox/* -> lightweight terraform testcases (fast apply/plan asserts)
- /tests/integration/* -> slower full-cluster/mesh scenarios (run on schedule)
- /examples/* -> curated example usage for users and reviewers
- /docs/compatibility.md -> human-readable compatibility notes auto-generated from the matrix below

Variables/outputs compatibility rules (short checklist):
- Never rename an existing output used by other modules; add new outputs with the new name and mark legacy outputs DEPRECATED in docs for at least one minor release.
- If changing the shape (map/list/object) of an output, require major version bump or provide both old+new outputs and a migration helper in examples.
- Avoid implicit behavior based on empty string vs null. Prefer explicit booleans or enums (e.g., enable_private_subnets = true/false).
- Inputs that change runtime semantics must be additive (new option) or gated behind a feature flag input with a default preserving legacy behavior.

Backwards-compatibility matrix (text representation):
Columns: component | variable/output | compatibility risk | recommended testcases | migration pattern
- VPC | cidr_block (input) | breaking if shape/format changes | testcase: apply with reserved-cidr + verify routes unchanged | migration: provide new input cidr_block_v2, map old -> new in wrapper module, document transition
- VPC | public_subnet_ids (output) | medium (name vs id) | testcase: create vpc + subnets, assert output includes expected ids | migration: keep old output, add public_subnet_ids_v2 with named map
- IAM | role_arn (output) | high (used by downstream) | testcase: module creates role, downstream attaches policy via reference | migration: add role_arn_v2, publish deprecation in changelog for 1 minor
- Cluster | kubeconfig (output) | high (consumed by tooling) | testcase: export kubeconfig, run kubectl get nodes | migration: continue kubeconfig, add kubeconfig_v2 with safer quick-parse fields
- Cluster | node_count (input) | low | testcase: scale node_count up/down and assert node readiness | migration: additive only (support min/max fields)

Recommended sandbox testcases (fast, ~5-7 minutes each):
1) VPC minimal create and idempotency
- Inputs: vpc_name=test-vpc, cidr=10.200.0.0/16, public_subnet_cidrs=[10.200.1.0/24]
- Asserts: terraform plan returns no changes on second apply, output.vpc_id exists, output.public_subnet_ids length==1, route table has expected IGW route (cloud-specific check).

2) IAM role drift / policy attachment smoke
- Inputs: role_name=test-role, attach_managed_policies=[], inline_policies=[minimal-s3-read]
- Asserts: role arn stable after apply, policy xhr-check via cloud API shows policy attached, terraform destroy removes role.

3) Cluster bootstrap and kubeconfig verification (cloud + kind fallback)
- Inputs: cluster_name=test-cluster, node_count=1, network_module reference -> use pre-created sandbox vpc outputs
- Asserts: kubeconfig present in outputs, kubectl --kubeconfig get nodes returns Ready nodes within 90s, node taints/labels match expected.

4) Output shape contract test (contract test harness)
- Pump mock upstream module that expects a specific output shape (e.g., public_subnet_map = { "us-west-1": ["subnet-abc"] })
- Run integration: change real module to add new output; ensure old mock consumer still reads legacy output.

5) Canary upgrade scenario (upgrade path test)
- Start with module version v1.2.3 -> apply test infra.
- Upgrade to branch under test (e.g., feature/rename-output) by pointing at local module path or git ref.
- Run plan and automated asserts that detect added/removed outputs and either fail (if breaking) or ensure legacy outputs present (if migration implemented).

Test harness recommendations and tooling:
- Use terratest (go) for runtime asserts where kubectl/cloud APIs are needed; use lightweight shell + terraform for pure-plan asserts.
- CI steps: terraform init -> terraform apply -auto-approve -> run asserts -> terraform destroy -auto-approve. Keep state files ephemeral and use unique prefixes (test-<commit>-<matrix-id>).
- For speed, use provider mocks for parts of the test that are expensive (e.g., simulate managed policies) but ensure at least one real-provider run per PR or nightly build.
- Maintain a small library of helper scripts: test/ci/terraform-wrap.sh (handles locking), test/ci/verify-output-json.sh (asserts shapes), test/ci/kube-ready-check.sh.

Upgrade and migration playbook (practical checklist):
- Step 0: add compatibility notes to module README (what changed, why, quick migration snippet).
- Step 1: add new outputs/inputs preserving legacy names where possible; mark deprecated in doc and add acceptance tests.
- Step 2: run sandbox canary upgrade tests (above) against 2 representative sandbox clusters (one AWS, one GCP/Azure or local kind).
- Step 3: publish release with CHANGELOG entry and migration guide; create PR to downstream wrapper modules to consume new outputs (if applicable).
- Step 4: monitor real-customer usage (telemetry) for two weeks if possible; provide rollback plan (pin old version and run terraform apply).
- Step 5: after one minor release cycle, remove deprecated outputs if no consumers (major version required for removal otherwise).

State migration notes (terraform state):
- Avoid moving resources across modules unless absolutely necessary. If a rename is required, provide a terraform state mv example in the upgrade guide and a tested script in /tools/state-migrations/.
- For output renames that require moving attributes, provide shim outputs that read from either old resource or new resource to avoid breaking downstream state references.

Edge cases and cloud specific notes:
- AWS: subnet az ordering can change; do not rely on index-of-subnets for stable mapping. Use tags+filters to produce stable maps in outputs.
- GKE: node pool autoscaler interacts with node_count; test with autoscaling disabled for deterministic asserts.
- AKS: cluster creation can surface long-lived network resource provisioning delays; CI should have longer timeouts or use an already-prewarmer cluster.
- On-prem: kubeadm/kind scenarios should test kubeconfig parsing differences (certificate expiry, context names). Provide an example wrapper to normalize kubeconfig into a small JSON (kube_meta) for downstream consumers.

Acceptance criteria for a module change touching public schema:
- Unit/contract tests for new behavior commit to repo and run green in CI.
- Sandbox canary suite green for at least 2 runs across different cloud providers or local + cloud combination.
- README updated with migration steps and deprecation notes for at least one minor release window.
- Changelog entry + related Jira ticket closed.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want an automated detector that scans terraform plans for "removed outputs" and blocks merges? (proto: cli tool that compares previous release plan vs new plan).
- Establish a canonical consumer registry so we can detect who consumes which outputs across internal repos.
- Timebox: add state migration test scripts for the top 10 most-modified modules by Q2 2025.

Appendix: quick example snippets
- Example: add safe-output shim
  output "public_subnet_ids_v2" {
    value = module.vpc.public_subnet_ids
  }

  output "public_subnet_ids" {
    value = try(module.vpc.public_subnet_ids, module.legacy_vpc.public_subnet_ids)
    description = "DEPRECATED - use public_subnet_ids_v2 (kept for backwards compatibility)"
  }

- Example: test runner invocation (CI)
  export TF_VAR_prefix=test-$(echo $GITHUB_SHA | cut -c1-7)
  pushd tests/sandbox/vpc-minimal
  terraform init -backend=false
  terraform apply -auto-approve
  ./../../test/ci/verify-output-json.sh state.tfstate public_subnet_ids 1
  terraform destroy -auto-approve

Notes for reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive and pragmatic—focus on making small changes to CI and adding one or two sandbox testcases per PR that touches public outputs.
- Suggest adding a lightweight pre-merge check that runs the plan-level compatibility detector (open question above).

Last edited by Aisha Patel on 2025-02-01.
